stem: A passenger sitting in a train A moving at $90$ km/h observes another train B moving in the opposite direction for $8$ s. If the velocity of the train B is $54$ km/h, then length of train B is:
solution:
$V_A = 90 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 25$ m/s, $V_B = 54 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 15$ m/s

Velocity of train B w.r.t. train A $= \vec{V}_B - \vec{V}_A = 15 - (-25) = 40$ m/s

$$\text{Time of crossing} = \frac{\text{length of train}}{\text{relative velocity}} \Rightarrow 8 = \frac{\ell}{40} \Rightarrow \ell = 320\ \text{m}$$

stem: The engine of a train moving with speed $10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ towards a platform sounds a whistle at frequency $400$ Hz. The frequency heard by a passenger inside the train is (neglect air speed. Speed of sound in air $330\ \text{m s}^{-1}$)
solution: The relative velocity of the passenger with respect to the source of sound (engine) is zero, so there is no Doppler effect. Frequency heard is $400$ Hz.

stem: If $V$ is the gravitational potential due to sphere of uniform density on its surface, then its value at the center of sphere will be:
A capacitor of capacitance $C$ is charged to a potential $V$. The flux of the electric field through a closed surface enclosing the positive plate of the capacitor is:
Eight equal drops of water are falling through air with a steady speed of $10$ cm/s. If the drops coalesce, the new velocity is:-
solution:
Terminal velocity $v \propto r^2$, so $\dfrac{v_1}{v_2} = \left(\dfrac{r}{R}\right)^2$

$$8 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \Rightarrow R = 2r$$

$$\frac{10}{v_2} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 \Rightarrow v_2 = 40\ \text{cm/s}$$

options: Gangue is an ore contaminated with undesired materials.
The scientific and technological process used for isolation of the metal from its ore is known as metallurgy.
Minerals are naturally occurring chemical substances in the earth's crust.

solution: Gangue is the commercially worthless material which contaminates the ore (it is not the ore itself).
